Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the network-adequacy disclosure set (access plan summary, provider directory notice, out-of-network cost-share notice, provider-termination and continuity-of-care letters) inside every Medical & Health EOC, certificate and correspondence template; escalates drafting calls to Regulatory Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — NAIC Model #74 network adequacy, provider directory and access plan sections, plus 45 CFR 156.230 and 156.245 for the QHP block, re-read at each form change; representative state Alaska AS 21.07.020/.030 and the Alaska Division of Insurance health filing instructions, with Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona network adequacy standards read for variant language

In-scope processes.value: Medical & Health product change intake to form/letter drafting to SERFF form filing to correspondence-library release — every EOC, certificate, member handbook, provider directory disclaimer page and network-change letter that carries a network adequacy disclosure, in all 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: SERFF for the form filings and each state's Filing Rules page; approved templates land in the policy administration correspondence library and the form inventory register

Compliance procedure documented.value: Network Adequacy Disclosure Drafting Procedure — obligation-to-artifact mapping table, per-state variant rules, mandatory language blocks, readability and taglines check, counsel review, SERFF submission and correspondence-library release

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel; re-approved on any state network adequacy bulletin and at minimum on each annual EOC refresh cycle

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per change — no day count in the source text, so the driver is the state review period backed off the plan year effective date (1 January for individual/small group); disclosure forms must be SERFF-submitted no later than the state's form filing cut-off for the plan year, commonly 1 May to 1 July of the preceding year

Deadline reminders configured.value: Form inventory milestone alerts at T-120/T-60/T-30 days to the plan year effective date on every disclosure artifact flagged 'network adequacy', plus an alert on any state bulletin tagged network adequacy in the regulatory change feed

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Form inventory extract, drafted and approved template PDFs with form number and edition date, per-state requirement mapping, counsel sign-off and SERFF disposition letters retained 10 years from withdrawal of the form edition

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A disclosure shipped without the required Model #74 language, or an edition used before its SERFF disposition, is logged as a form defect with impacted member count, corrective mailing and refile date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off each corrected disclosure edition and any decision not to re-issue a defective notice to members already enrolled

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every Medical & Health form and correspondence template with a network adequacy disclosure that was created or amended in the plan year, taken from the form inventory register by form number, edition date, state and product

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on missing mandatory language blocks and on use-before-approval; content defects that do not change member rights are capped at 2 percent of the sample before the whole edition is recalled

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per change, so the test runs each time a disclosure edition is released plus a full sweep of the form inventory before the 1 January plan year

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted, reviewed or filed any sampled form edition

Evidence location for test results.value: Disclosure content test workpaper (inventory extract, per-state mapping, marked-up template copies, SERFF dispositions, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-036-C01 and the plan year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Form inventory export showing form number, edition date, state, SERFF tracking number and disposition date, with the approved PDF for each row, producible for a market conduct exam form request within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager owns replies to Division form objections and exam form criticisms; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission that an unapproved disclosure edition was issued to members

checklist.step: Take in the network or product change that triggers a disclosure rewrite
actions: Open the product change queue and filter Line of Business = Medical & Health, Status = 'Approved for build', Change type in (network build, tier change, plan design, service area).
Ask the Insurance Product Manager for the network id, the counties or ZIP-3 service area being added or dropped, the plan year effective date and whether in-force members are affected.
Open a disclosure worksheet named <plan year>-<network id>-<state list> and paste those attributes into the header.
Attach the signed change request and the network build sheet from Provider Network Operations to the worksheet folder.
checklist.done: the worksheet carries network id, service area, plan year effective date, in-force impact flag and the signed change request.

checklist.step: Map each Model 74 disclosure obligation to a named form or letter
actions: List the disclosure obligations on separate worksheet rows: access plan availability statement, provider directory availability and accuracy statement, time/distance and appointment wait time standards summary, referral rules when no participating provider is reasonably available, cost sharing applied at the in-network level for such referrals, provider termination notice, continuity of care rights, and the complaint/appeal route for access denials.
Against each row write the artifact that will carry it: EOC section number, certificate page, member handbook chapter, directory disclaimer page, or the letter code in the correspondence library.
Mark rows where no artifact exists today as GAP and assign a drafting owner and date.
Send the mapping to Regulatory Counsel for a first read before drafting starts.
checklist.done: every obligation row names a specific artifact and section, with GAP rows owned and dated.

checklist.step: Pull each state's variant disclosure requirements from SERFF filing rules
actions: Log in to SERFF with the company industry instance and open Industry then Filing Rules.

Select the state, Business Type = Health, and the TOI/Sub-TOI for the product (for example H16I Individual Health - Major Medical), then open the General Instructions and any attached health network adequacy or access plan checklist.
Read Alaska first as the representative jurisdiction (AS 21.07.020/.030 and the Division's health filing checklist), then Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona, then the remaining states.
Copy each state-specific demand onto the worksheet: mandatory sentence, font or placement rule, notice day count, required Spanish or other tagline, and the cite it comes from.
Print each instructions page to PDF as <state>-network-adequacy-form-rules-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and file it in the worksheet folder.
checklist.done: a dated filing-rules capture and a variant list exist for all 51 jurisdictions in the worksheet folder.

checklist.step: Draft the access plan and network standards disclosure into the EOC and certificate
actions: Open the current EOC master in the document repository and check out the 'How to get care from network providers' section.
Insert the statement that the access plan is filed with the Division and available on request and on the member site, with the phone number and URL spelled out.

State the network adequacy standards in member language: maximum travel time and distance to a primary care provider and to each specialty tier, and the appointment wait time standards for urgent, routine and preventive visits.

State that where no participating provider meets those standards the member may use a non-participating provider at the in-network cost share, and name the pre-authorization step and phone number to arrange it.
Assign the new edition date to the form footer and check the section back in with a change note referencing the worksheet id.
checklist.done: the EOC section states the access plan availability, the time/distance and wait time standards and the in-network cost share rule for out-of-network referrals, under a new edition date.

checklist.step: Draft the provider directory disclosure and accuracy statement
actions: Draft the directory disclaimer block: the date the directory was last updated, that the online directory is updated at least monthly, that provider participation and panel-open status can change, and how to report an inaccuracy.
Add the statement that a member who relied on a directory listing that was wrong will be held to the in-network cost share for that service, and name the team that adjudicates such claims.
Add the print-directory request line: a paper directory is furnished on request at no charge within the state's stated turnaround.
Hand the block to Provider Network Operations to confirm the update cadence and the inaccuracy-reporting mailbox actually exist before it is published.
checklist.done: the directory disclaimer block carries the update cadence, the reliance protection, the inaccuracy-report route and a confirmed paper-copy channel.

checklist.step: Draft the provider termination and continuity of care letter templates
actions: Create letter codes for: participating provider termination, facility termination, and continuity of care offer.

In the termination letter include the provider name and specialty, the termination effective date, the fact that treatment after that date is out of network, at least two named alternative participating providers with addresses and phone numbers, and the transition request phone number.

In the continuity of care letter set out the qualifying conditions the state recognises (ongoing course of treatment, second or third trimester pregnancy through delivery and post-partum care, terminal illness) and the transitional period offered, using the state's day count and defaulting to 90 days where the state is silent.
Add the merge fields the letters need — member name, member id, group, provider name, termination date, transition end date — and list them for the Configuration Engineer.
Have a Medical / Nurse Case Manager read the continuity of care letter and confirm the clinical qualifying conditions and the request route are the ones the case management team can actually honour.
checklist.done: three letter templates exist with named alternative providers, the state transitional period and a merge-field list handed to configuration.

checklist.step: Run the readability and language access checks on every drafted artifact
actions: Run the Flesch Reading Ease score on each drafted section and letter and record the score on the worksheet row; rework anything below the state minimum, commonly 40 to 50 for health forms.

Check the artifact against the state's language access rule and add the taglines for each language spoken by 5 percent or more of the population in the service area, plus the TTY line and the interpreter phone number.
Confirm the notice of non-discrimination and auxiliary aids statement travels with each member-facing notice.
Log the score, the tagline languages used and the source of the language threshold on the worksheet row.
checklist.done: each artifact has a recorded Flesch score at or above the state minimum and a tagline set matched to its service area.

checklist.step: Get Regulatory Counsel to clear the language against the cited requirement
actions: Read each drafted block beside the requirement row and the dated filing-rules capture it was written from.
Confirm that mandatory sentences appear verbatim where the state demands verbatim text, and that paraphrase is only used where the state allows substantially similar language.
Reject any block that narrows a member right relative to the statute — in particular the cost share treatment for out-of-network referrals and the continuity of care period.
Stamp name and date on each cleared row; rejected rows go back to drafting the same week.
checklist.done: no artifact enters the filing package without a dated counsel clearance on every requirement row it carries.

checklist.step: Register the new editions in the form inventory
actions: Add one inventory row per artifact: form number, edition date, artifact type (EOC, certificate, handbook, directory page, letter code), product, network id, state list, obligation rows carried, and status = 'Drafted'.
Retire the superseded edition by setting its end date to the day before the new edition's effective date so the two never overlap.
Attach the counsel-cleared PDF and the requirement mapping to each inventory row.
Confirm the register search returns the row by form number, by state and by obligation tag 'network adequacy'.
checklist.done: the form inventory holds one dated, source-linked row per new edition with the superseded edition closed out.

checklist.step: Assemble and submit the state form filings in SERFF
actions: In SERFF create a new filing per state, select the company and NAIC co-code, Business Type = Health and the matching TOI/Sub-TOI, and set Filing Type per the state's review method.
On the Form Schedule tab add each artifact with its form number, edition date, form type and replaced form number, and attach the print-ready PDF plus the redline against the prior edition.

On the Supporting Documentation tab attach the readability certification, the statement of variability, the cover letter explaining the network adequacy disclosure change, and the access plan where the state's checklist demands it be filed with the forms.
Pay the state filing fee by EFT where the state requires it and record the confirmation on the worksheet.
Submit and write the SERFF tracking number back onto every form inventory row in the filing.
checklist.done: every state has a submitted SERFF form filing and every inventory row carries its SERFF tracking number.

checklist.step: Work the state objections until each filing reaches a disposition
actions: Check the SERFF Objection Letters tab daily and record each objection, its response due date and the reviewer's name on the worksheet.
Route wording objections to Policy Forms Specialist and legal-position objections to Regulatory Counsel, with an internal due date three business days before the state's date.
Respond through the SERFF Response tab, attaching the amended form with a new edition date where the wording changed, and note the amendment in the form inventory.
Record the final disposition (Approved, Filed, Acknowledged, Disapproved) and its date on the inventory row.
checklist.done: every filing shows a recorded disposition and date, and any amended edition is registered in the inventory.

checklist.step: Release the approved templates into the correspondence library
actions: Load each approved template into the correspondence library under its letter code with the approved edition date and the state list it is valid for.
Bind the merge fields listed by the Policy Forms Specialist and run a proof render for one member per state to confirm no field resolves blank.
Set the template's activation date to the state's approval or deemed date so the system cannot issue it earlier.
Deactivate the superseded template on the same date and confirm no workflow still points at it.
checklist.done: each approved template is live from its own state-specific activation date, proof-rendered, with the prior version deactivated.

checklist.step: Publish the state-by-state disclosure matrix to the operating teams
actions: Publish a matrix of state by artifact by edition date by SERFF tracking number by activation date.
Send it to Policy Administration, the contact centre, Provider Network Operations and Market Conduct with the note of what changed from the prior edition.
Add the changed sentences to the contact centre knowledge base article on network access so agents answer from the new text.
Book a 30-minute walkthrough with the contact centre supervisors before the activation date.
checklist.done: the matrix is published, distributed and reflected in the contact centre knowledge base before the earliest activation date.

checklist.step: Handle in-force members when the disclosure change alters an existing right
actions: Decide, with Regulatory Counsel, whether the change requires notice to members already enrolled rather than only to new issues.
Where it does, request the in-force member extract for the affected states and networks from Policy Administration and set the mailing date.
Where it does not, record the reasoning and the citation on the worksheet so the decision is defensible at exam.
Log either outcome as a decision row with owner and date.
checklist.done: a written, cited decision exists on in-force notification, with a mailing date where notification is required.

checklist.step: File the disclosure evidence set for the retention period
actions: Move the worksheet folder — requirement mapping, dated filing-rules captures, counsel clearances, approved PDFs, SERFF dispositions, readability certifications — into the evidence repository under REG-036-C01 and the plan year.
Apply the 10-years-from-edition-withdrawal retention label so the record outlives the plan year.
Confirm the record is indexed by form number, state, SERFF tracking number and obligation tag.
Send the repository location to the Regulatory Affairs Manager for the exam response pack.
checklist.done: the evidence set is filed, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by form number and state.

testing.step: Build the population of disclosure artifacts changed in the plan year
actions: Extract from the form inventory every row with obligation tag 'network adequacy' and an edition date inside the plan year, with form number, state, product, artifact type and SERFF tracking number.
Add the correspondence library export of letter codes and template versions so letters that never went through a form filing cannot hide.
Reconcile the two counts to the product change log for the year and resolve every difference before drawing a sample.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the product change log and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every live artifact to an approved SERFF disposition that pre-dates its use
actions: Match each population row to a SERFF filing on company, state, form number and edition date.
Compare the disposition date to the template activation date recorded in the correspondence library.
List any artifact activated before its disposition date, and any artifact with no filing at all, as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every artifact is matched to a pre-dated disposition or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample across states and artifact types
actions: Take 100 percent of the representative jurisdiction Alaska plus Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona rows.
Take 25 further rows at random using a recorded seed, forcing at least one EOC, one directory page and one letter code into the sample.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all four cited jurisdictions and every artifact type.

testing.step: Re-perform the requirement mapping against the state's current text
actions: Open SERFF Industry then Filing Rules for the sampled state and the health TOI as it stood on the artifact's edition date.
Read the network adequacy and access plan requirements and write your own list of mandatory disclosure elements before opening the compliance mapping.
Compare your list to the mapping; a missing element is an exception and so is an element mapped to an artifact the member never receives.
Screenshot the instructions page relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled state has an independent element list and a captured source page.

testing.step: Read the sampled artifact for the mandatory content blocks
actions: Open the approved PDF and tick off each element: access plan availability, time/distance standards, appointment wait time standards, out-of-network referral at in-network cost share, directory update cadence and inaccuracy route, termination notice content, continuity of care period, complaint route.
Check the mandatory-verbatim sentences match the state text character for character where verbatim is demanded.
Flag any block that states a shorter continuity of care period or a higher cost share than the statute allows as a member-rights defect rather than a wording issue.
testing.done: each sampled artifact has a completed element tick-list with every miss classified as wording or member-rights.

testing.step: Prove the version members actually received is the approved edition
actions: For five sampled letter codes pull three issued member copies each from the correspondence archive.
Compare the edition date and footer form number on the issued copy to the approved edition in the form inventory.
Open the member portal directory page for two sampled states and confirm the live disclaimer text matches the approved block, not a stale one.
Capture the issued copies and portal screens into the workpaper.
testing.done: every inspected issued copy and live page carries the approved form number and edition date.

testing.step: Recompute the readability score and the tagline threshold
actions: Re-run the Flesch Reading Ease calculation on the sampled artifact text and compare to the score recorded on the worksheet.
Recompute the language threshold from the service area population data and confirm every language at or above 5 percent has a tagline on the artifact.
Note any score below the state minimum or missing tagline language, with the difference from the recorded figure.
testing.done: recomputed scores and tagline languages agree with the recorded values or the difference is quantified.

testing.step: Test that counsel clearance and the inventory trail are complete
actions: Pull the counsel clearance for each sampled edition and confirm it is dated before the SERFF submission date.
Confirm the superseded edition was end-dated the day before the new edition's activation so no overlap exists.
Confirm the dated filing-rules capture behind the mapping exists and is from the same drafting cycle, not carried over from a prior year.
Treat a clearance dated after submission as an exception even where the content is correct.
testing.done: every sampled edition has a pre-dated clearance, a closed-out predecessor and a same-cycle rules capture.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception carrying form number, state, the element missed and the count of members who received the defective artifact.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: mapping missed the element, stale state rules capture, drafting error, filed but not activated, activated before approval.
Set a remediation date and, where a member-rights defect shipped, open a corrective mailing and a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open issue into the next release test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the disclosure content test
actions: Compute the defect rate against the zero-tolerance rule for missing mandatory blocks and the 2 percent cap for wording defects.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted, cleared or filed none of the sampled editions, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any member-rights defect to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, defect rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — NAIC Model #74 provider termination and continuity of care sections read against each state's day count; representative Alaska AS 21.07.030 and the Alaska Division of Insurance health bulletins, with Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona network adequacy standards checked for shorter notice windows

In-scope processes.value: Provider roster termination feed to impacted-member identification to notice generation to print and e-delivery to return-mail handling to notice log closure, for Medical & Health members in all 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: Policy admin correspondence engine drives generation and the notice log; the provider roster feed and claims attribution identify impacted members; the print/mail vendor returns the mailed-on date

Compliance procedure documented.value: Network Change Member Notification Procedure — trigger definitions, member attribution rules (PCP assignment plus 12 months of claims with the terminating provider), day-count table by state, generation batch schedule, undeliverable handling and log closure

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with the Contact Center Ops Manager countersigning the call-handling annex; reviewed on any change to a state notice day count

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven — no day count in the source text, so the operating rule is the state's own window, defaulting to notice mailed at least 30 calendar days before the provider's termination effective date, or within 15 calendar days of the carrier learning of a termination it received late

Deadline reminders configured.value: Daily aging report on open notice events at T-45, T-35 and T-31 days to the termination effective date, with a same-day page to the Policy Admin Ops Lead on any event inside T-31 without a mailed-on date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Notice log rows with member id, event id, generation timestamp, mailed-on date from the vendor manifest, the rendered PDF copy and any return-mail disposition, retained 10 years from the notice date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any notice mailed inside the state window, not mailed at all, or returned undeliverable without a second attempt is raised as a late-notice case with member count, remediation mailing and continuity of care offer extension

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Compliance signs off each late-notice remediation package, including the decision on whether the affected members get an extended transitional care period

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every provider and facility termination event with an effective date in the quarter, joined to the impacted-member list, plus every continuity of care offer and out-of-network referral approval issued in the quarter

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 98 percent of notices mailed on or before the state deadline; any single member with no notice at all, or any missed continuity of care offer for a pregnancy or terminal illness case, is an automatic fail regardless of the rate

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven, so a daily automated aging control runs continuously and a quarterly sample-based test re-performs the day-count and delivery evidence

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Policy Administration and must not have generated or released any sampled notice batch

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly notice timeliness workpaper (event extract, attribution reconciliation, day-count recomputation, vendor manifests, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-036-C02

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Notice log export by state and event with mailed-on dates and rendered copies, matching the MCAS Health and market conduct exam notice request format, producible within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager answers Division inquiries about a specific member's notice; Regulatory Counsel clears any response conceding a missed statutory notice

checklist.step: Receive the provider termination feed and open a notice event
actions: Pull the daily provider roster delta from Provider Network Operations and filter Action = Terminate on provider, group or facility records.
For each row capture provider NPI, tax id, specialty, all practice locations, the termination effective date and the date the carrier was notified.
Open a notice event per terminating provider per state and set Event date received = the carrier notification date, since that is what the late-notice clock runs from.
Reject roster rows missing an effective date or an NPI back to Provider Network Operations the same day rather than holding them in a queue.
checklist.done: every terminate row has an open notice event with NPI, effective date and carrier notification date, or is rejected back to the source the same day.

checklist.step: Identify the members who must be notified
actions: Run the impacted-member query: all active members with the terminating provider recorded as assigned PCP, plus all members with a paid or pending claim to that provider NPI in the last 12 months, plus members with an open authorization referencing the provider.
De-duplicate to one row per member per event and attach member id, plan, state of issue, mailing address, e-delivery consent flag and preferred language.
Hand a count-by-state summary to the Policy Admin Ops Lead and note any event with zero impacted members so the zero is deliberate rather than a failed join.
Load the member list against the notice event in the correspondence queue.
checklist.done: each event carries a de-duplicated impacted-member list with address, delivery preference and language, or a documented zero.

checklist.step: Compute the mail-by date for each event from the state rule
actions: Look up the state on the notice day-count table and read its advance-notice requirement for provider terminations.
Compute mail-by date = termination effective date minus the state day count, and compute the late-notification alternative = carrier notification date plus 15 calendar days.
Set the event's mail-by date to the earlier of the two and write both inputs onto the event so the maths can be re-performed.
Where the computed mail-by date is already in the past, flag the event RED to the Policy Admin Ops Lead before generation rather than after.
checklist.done: every event shows both computed dates, the governing mail-by date and a RED flag where it is already unreachable.

checklist.step: Generate the notices from the approved template
actions: Select the letter code for the event type (provider termination, facility termination, continuity of care offer) and confirm the template edition is the one active for that state.

Run the merge and check the proof render for the first three members: provider name and specialty, termination effective date, the two named alternative participating providers with addresses and distances, the transition request phone number and the appeals route must all populate.
Reject the batch where any merge field renders blank or shows a placeholder, and raise it to the Configuration Engineer rather than hand-editing letters.
Release the batch with a batch id and record the generation timestamp on every notice log row.
checklist.done: the batch is released with no blank merge fields and every log row carries the batch id and generation timestamp.

checklist.step: Source the named alternative providers that go into each letter
actions: For each impacted member run the nearest-participating-provider query on the same specialty, filtered to accepting-new-patients status.
Return the two closest by driving distance from the member's mailing address and check both meet the plan's time and distance standard for that specialty and county type.
Where no participating provider meets the standard, tag the member NO-ADEQUATE-ALTERNATIVE and route to the out-of-network referral path instead of a plain termination letter.
Pass the provider pairs back into the merge file keyed on member id.
checklist.done: every letter names two accepting, in-standard alternatives, or the member is tagged NO-ADEQUATE-ALTERNATIVE and routed to the referral path.

checklist.step: Hand the print batch to the mail vendor and capture the mailed-on date
actions: Transmit the print file to the vendor with the batch id, the required mail class and the mail-by date on the job ticket.
Require the vendor manifest back within one business day carrying piece count, postmark date and any pieces suppressed for bad address.
Reconcile manifest piece count to the batch member count and chase any difference the same day.
Write the postmark date into the notice log as mailed-on date — never the generation date.
checklist.done: the manifest reconciles to the batch count and every log row carries a vendor postmark date.

checklist.step: Deliver electronically where the member has consented
actions: Split the batch on the e-delivery consent flag and confirm the consent is current and covers regulatory notices, not only billing.
Post the notice to the member document centre and send the notification email with the subject line naming the provider and the termination date.
Capture the post timestamp and the email delivery or bounce status onto the log row.
Fall back to paper within one business day for any bounce or any member whose consent has lapsed.
checklist.done: each e-delivered notice has a post timestamp and a delivered status, with bounces converted to paper within one business day.

checklist.step: Make the continuity of care offer to members in active treatment
actions: Filter the impacted-member list to open authorizations, active care plans, second or third trimester pregnancy and terminal illness flags.

Open a case per member and issue the continuity of care offer letter stating the transitional period the state grants, defaulting to 90 days, and through delivery plus post-partum care for pregnancy cases.
Call each pregnancy and terminal illness member within two business days of the letter and record the contact attempt on the case.
Load the accepted transitional period into the authorization so claims price at the in-network benefit for its duration.
checklist.done: every active-treatment member has a case, an issued offer, a logged contact attempt for high-acuity cases and an authorization carrying the transitional period.

checklist.step: Write the notice log row and close the event
actions: Complete each log row: event id, member id, state, notice type, letter code and edition, mail-by date, generation timestamp, mailed-on date, delivery channel and status.
Compute days-early = mail-by date minus mailed-on date on the row so lateness is visible without recalculation.
Set event status to Closed only when every member row has a mailed-on or delivered date.
Leave RED events open and visible on the aging report until remediated.
checklist.done: the log holds one complete row per member per event with a days-early figure and no event closed with an unmailed member.

checklist.step: Work the daily aging report before events go late
actions: Open the notice aging dashboard each morning and read the buckets T-45, T-35, T-31 and past-due.
Chase every T-35 event to a released batch the same day; escalate every T-31 event to the Compliance Officer by close of business.
Record the reason for each past-due event — late roster feed, failed attribution, template not active for the state, vendor delay — directly on the event.
Publish the past-due count and reasons to Compliance weekly.
checklist.done: no event passes T-31 without an escalation, and every past-due event carries a recorded reason.

checklist.step: Handle returned and undeliverable mail
actions: Load the vendor's return-mail file daily and match each piece back to its notice log row.
Run the returned address through the address-correction service and the most recent claim or premium payment record for a better address.
Re-mail within three business days to the corrected address and record the second mailed-on date on the row.
Where no better address exists, place an outbound call and a portal message, and record both attempts before marking the row Undeliverable.
checklist.done: every returned piece is either re-mailed with a new date or marked Undeliverable behind two recorded alternative attempts.

checklist.step: Arm the contact centre for the calls the notices will generate
actions: Load the impacted-member list into the screen-pop so an agent sees the termination and the transitional period before answering.
Publish the call script covering how to find another participating provider, how to request continuity of care, and when the out-of-network in-network cost share applies.
Add a disposition code for network-access calls tied to the event id so volumes can be trended against the mailings.
Staff the forecast uplift for the ten business days following the largest mail drop.
checklist.done: the screen-pop, script, disposition code and staffing uplift are live before the mail drop lands.

checklist.step: Route members with no adequate alternative to the out-of-network referral path
actions: Take the NO-ADEQUATE-ALTERNATIVE list and open a referral case per member.
Approve the out-of-network provider at the in-network cost share, load the authorization and state the approved period and services on it.
Send the member the referral approval letter naming the approved provider, the cost share that applies and the renewal route.
Notify Provider Network Operations of every county and specialty generating these referrals so the network gap is fed back into recruitment.
checklist.done: every no-alternative member holds an authorization at the in-network cost share and the gap is reported to network recruitment.

checklist.step: Escalate and remediate any notice that missed the state window
actions: Open a late-notice case for each event with a negative days-early figure, listing member count, state and the number of days late.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether the transitional care period is extended by the days lost and instruct Case Management accordingly.
Issue the corrective notice with a plain explanation of the delay and the extended dates.
Record whether a self-report to the Division is required and the date it was filed.
checklist.done: every late event has a case, a member remediation, a documented self-report decision and an owner.

checklist.step: Retain the notice evidence for the retention period
actions: Archive the notice log extract, rendered PDF copies, vendor manifests and return-mail dispositions per quarter into the evidence repository under REG-036-C02.
Apply the 10-years-from-notice-date retention label.
Confirm the archive is searchable by member id, provider NPI, state and event id, which is how an exam request will arrive.
Confirm a rendered copy opens for a spot-checked member before signing the archive off.
checklist.done: the quarter's notice evidence is archived, labelled and retrievable by member id and provider NPI.

testing.step: Build the population of notice events for the quarter
actions: Extract every provider and facility termination with an effective date in the quarter from the provider roster history, independently of the notice log.
Extract every continuity of care case and out-of-network referral approval opened in the quarter.
Reconcile the roster-derived event count to the notice log event count and investigate every event present in the roster but absent from the log before sampling.
testing.done: the roster-derived population reconciles to the notice log and unmatched events are listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Reconcile the impacted-member attribution to the source of record
actions: For five sampled events re-run the attribution independently: PCP assignment plus 12 months of paid or pending claims to the provider NPI plus open authorizations.
Compare your member count to the count on the notice event and list every member you found who received no notice.
Check the de-duplication did not drop members holding two coverages, which is the usual cause of a silent under-count.
testing.done: the re-performed member counts agree with the event counts or every missed member is listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of member notices
actions: Take 100 percent of RED and late events, all continuity of care cases for pregnancy and terminal illness, and all Alaska events as the representative jurisdiction.
Take 40 further member notice rows at random with a recorded seed, spread across at least ten states.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every late event and every high-acuity continuity of care case.

testing.step: Recompute the mail-by date for each sampled row
actions: Read the state day count from the current statute or bulletin rather than from the internal day-count table, and note the cite.
Recompute mail-by date = termination effective date minus the state day count, and the alternative = carrier notification date plus 15 days, then take the earlier.
Compare your date to the recorded mail-by date and to the actual mailed-on date, and record the days-early figure yourself.
Flag any row where the internal table understates the state requirement — that is a systemic finding, not a single-row exception.
testing.done: every sampled row has an independently recomputed mail-by date and days-early figure with the state cite recorded.

testing.step: Trace each sampled notice to a vendor postmark or delivery record
actions: Open the vendor manifest for the batch and locate the piece by member id, then read the postmark date.
For e-delivered rows open the portal audit record and read the post timestamp and the email delivery status.
Confirm the log's mailed-on date equals the postmark or post timestamp and is not the generation date.
Capture the manifest line and the portal audit record into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled notice traces to an independent postmark or delivery record matching the logged date.

testing.step: Read the delivered notice content against the approved template
actions: Open the rendered member copy and check it carries the provider name and specialty, the termination effective date, two named alternative participating providers with addresses, the transition request number and the appeals route.
Confirm the letter edition and form number match the edition approved for that state on the mailing date.
Re-run the nearest-provider query for two sampled members and confirm the named alternatives were accepting new patients and inside the time and distance standard.
Treat a named alternative who was closed to new patients as a content failure.
testing.done: every sampled copy carries the required content and its named alternatives verify as in-standard and open.

testing.step: Test the continuity of care offers and the resulting claim pricing
actions: For each sampled continuity of care case confirm the offer letter was issued and the transitional period matches the state requirement, defaulting to 90 days.
Pull the claims paid to the terminated provider inside the transitional period and confirm they priced at the in-network benefit level.
Confirm pregnancy cases ran through delivery plus post-partum care rather than stopping at a flat day count.
List any claim that member-cost-shared at out-of-network rates as a member harm exception with the dollar amount.
testing.done: every transitional claim priced in-network or the member harm is quantified in dollars.

testing.step: Test return-mail and undeliverable handling
actions: Pull all rows marked Undeliverable in the quarter and check each shows an address-correction attempt plus two alternative contact attempts before the mark.
Confirm re-mails happened inside three business days of the return-mail file load.
Check whether the corrected address later appeared on a claim or premium record before the mark, which would show the search was not run.
testing.done: every Undeliverable row is supported by a correction attempt and two logged alternative attempts.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a case per exception carrying event id, member ids, days late and the member impact in dollars or in denied access.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: roster feed late, attribution query missed members, day-count table wrong, template inactive for the state, vendor delay, return-mail not worked.
Set the remediation date and the corrective mailing scope, and record the self-report decision cleared by Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open case into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a case, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the notice timeliness test
actions: Compute the on-time notice rate against the 98 percent threshold and list every automatic-fail condition triggered.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper sections behind it.
Have the independent reviewer from outside Policy Administration sign the workpaper.
Report the rate, the member harm total and open self-reports to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, on-time rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Take the disclosure and timing rules in as configuration requirements
actions: Raise a configuration story per jurisdiction rule change referencing the Compliance requirements sheet row and its citation.

For each row capture: notice type, trigger event, day count, whether the count is calendar or business days, the count anchor (termination effective date or carrier notification date), and the template letter code.
Send back to the Compliance Analyst any row where the anchor or the day-count basis is ambiguous — never guess calendar versus business days.
Attach the requirements sheet to the story and link it to the epic for REG-036 network adequacy.
checklist.done: every rule change has a story with notice type, trigger, anchor, day-count basis, template code and citation, with no ambiguous rows in build.

checklist.step: Build the jurisdiction rules table with one row per state per notice type
actions: Open the correspondence rules maintenance screen and create or amend the row keyed on jurisdiction code plus notice type.
Populate day count, day-count basis, anchor field, effective-from date, effective-to date, template letter code and the citation text field.
Never overwrite an existing row — end-date it and insert the new row so the historic rule stays available to re-perform a past notice.
Confirm all 51 jurisdictions carry a row for each of the three notice types with no nulls in day count or template code.
checklist.done: the table holds effective-dated rows for all 51 jurisdictions and every notice type, with the prior rows end-dated rather than overwritten.

checklist.step: Wire the trigger events so notices cannot depend on a person remembering
actions: Configure the provider roster inbound interface to raise a NOTICE_EVENT record on any Terminate action, carrying NPI, effective date and carrier notification timestamp.
Configure the attribution job to run on event creation and write the impacted-member set to the event, and to fail the event loudly where the job returns zero rows for a provider with paid claims.
Configure the mail-by date calculation to read the jurisdiction rules row effective on the event date, not the current row.
Set the event to block manual closure while any member row lacks a mailed-on date.
checklist.done: a roster termination automatically creates an event with an attributed member set and a rules-derived mail-by date, and cannot be closed with unmailed members.

checklist.step: Bind the approved templates and their merge fields
actions: Load each Compliance-approved template into the correspondence library under its letter code with the approved edition date and the state list it is valid for.

Map every merge field: member name, member id, plan, provider name, specialty, termination effective date, transition end date, alternative provider one and two with address and phone, transition request number and appeals address.
Set the engine to abort the batch, not print a blank, where any mandatory merge field resolves null.
Set the template activation date to the state approval date so an unapproved edition cannot be issued.
checklist.done: each template is bound with all mandatory merge fields, aborts on null, and activates only from its state approval date.

checklist.step: Add the audit columns the notice log needs to be evidence
actions: Extend the notice log with generation timestamp, batch id, template code and edition, jurisdiction rule id used, computed mail-by date, mailed-on date from the vendor manifest, delivery channel, delivery status and return-mail disposition.
Make mailed-on date writable only by the vendor manifest load job so no one can type a date that beats the postmark.
Add a computed days-early column so lateness is visible without recalculation.
Turn on row-level change history for the log so any edit is attributable.
checklist.done: the notice log carries all audit columns, a system-written mailed-on date and row-level change history.

checklist.step: Build the aging and exception reporting off the configured data
actions: Build the daily notice aging dataset with buckets T-45, T-35, T-31 and past-due, sliced by state, notice type and event.
Build the exception view listing events with negative days-early, blank mailed-on dates, aborted batches and Undeliverable rows.
Schedule the refresh for 06:00 local so the Policy Admin Ops Lead sees it before the working day.
Configure the alert that pages the Policy Admin Ops Lead and copies the Compliance Officer on any event entering past-due.
checklist.done: the aging dashboard and exception view refresh daily at 06:00 with a working past-due alert.

checklist.step: Write the dated test scenarios that prove the rules bite
actions: Write one scenario per jurisdiction rule: termination dated far in the future, termination notified late so the notification-plus-15 rule governs, and termination inside the window so the event must flag RED.
Add scenarios for a null merge field, a member with two coverages, a member with a claim but no PCP assignment, and a state whose template is not yet activated.
State the expected mail-by date and expected system behaviour on every scenario before running it.
Store the pack in the test repository so the same pack reruns on every release.
checklist.done: a stored scenario pack covers all 51 jurisdiction rules and the six edge cases with stated expected results.

checklist.step: Run the scenario pack and the regression suite
actions: Execute the pack in the test environment with the system date set to each scenario's date so the effective-dated rule lookup is genuinely exercised.
Record actual mail-by date, generated template code and edition, and system behaviour against expected for every scenario.
Rerun the wider correspondence regression suite to prove no other letter type broke.
Raise a defect for every mismatch and block the release while any defect on a jurisdiction rule row is open.
checklist.done: every scenario passes with actuals matching expected, the regression suite is green and no jurisdiction-rule defect is open.

checklist.step: Put the configuration through Compliance UAT
actions: Re-perform ten jurisdiction rows straight off the requirements sheet in the UAT environment, including Alaska, Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona.
Open the generated PDF for each and read it against the approved template rather than only checking that a file appeared.
Sign the UAT record naming the rows tested, the defects found and their resolution.
Withhold sign-off where any day count or template edition differs from the requirements sheet, whatever the release pressure.
checklist.done: a signed Compliance UAT record exists naming the tested rows and confirming day counts and template editions match the requirements sheet.

checklist.step: Release through change control with a back-out plan
actions: Raise the change record referencing the stories, the test evidence and the Compliance UAT sign-off, and classify it as regulatory.
Attach the pre-change rules table export as the back-out artifact and state the back-out steps and the decision point.
Schedule the deployment window so it lands at least five business days before the earliest state rule effective date.
Take CAB approval with the Compliance Manager recorded as an approver, not an informed party.
checklist.done: an approved change record exists with test evidence, Compliance UAT sign-off, a back-out export and a window ahead of the rule effective date.

checklist.step: Verify the configuration in production the same day it deploys
actions: Export the production jurisdiction rules table and diff it against the intended post-change export row by row.
Generate one proof notice per changed state against a test member and confirm the mail-by date and the template edition are correct.
Confirm the daily aging job and the past-due alert both ran after deployment.
Attach the diff and the proof notices to the change record before closing it.
checklist.done: the production table diff is clean, proof notices render correctly and the evidence is attached to the change record.

checklist.step: Lock down who can change the rules table
actions: Restrict write access on the jurisdiction rules table and the correspondence template library to the configuration role only, and remove standing production write from analysts.
Require an approved change record id on any production write, enforced by the platform's maintenance screen.
Certify the entitlement quarterly and remove anyone who has not used it.
Feed the table's change history into the SIEM so an out-of-change edit alerts.
checklist.done: only the configuration role holds write access, every write ties to a change record and out-of-change edits alert.

checklist.step: Document the configuration baseline so it can be re-performed
actions: Publish the baseline page: table structures, the 51 jurisdiction rows with citations, trigger definitions, template bindings and the report definitions.
Link each row to the Compliance requirements sheet row and to the change record that created it.
Version the page on every release and keep the prior version accessible.
Name the current owner and the review date on the page header.
checklist.done: a versioned baseline page exists linking every configured row to a requirement and a change record.

checklist.step: Monitor the running configuration for silent failure
actions: Configure alerts for: the roster interface delivering zero termination rows for two consecutive days, the attribution job returning zero members for a provider with paid claims, an aborted correspondence batch, and a vendor manifest not loaded within 24 hours.
Route each alert to the on-call queue with a one-business-day response target and copy the Policy Admin Ops Lead.
Review the alert log weekly for suppressed or repeatedly acknowledged alerts, which hide a real break.
Raise a problem record where the same alert fires three times in a month.
checklist.done: the four silent-failure alerts are live, routed and reviewed weekly, with repeats raised as problem records.

checklist.step: Retain the configuration evidence for the retention period
actions: Copy the requirements sheet, before and after rules exports, scenario results, UAT sign-off, change record and post-deploy diff into the evidence repository under REG-036-C03 and the release id.
Apply the 7-years-from-supersession retention label.
Confirm the record is indexed by release id, jurisdiction and change record id.
Confirm the historic rules export opens so a past notice can be re-performed against the rule that was live at the time.
checklist.done: the release evidence is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and the historic rules export is retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of configuration items and changes
actions: Export the full jurisdiction rules table with effective dates and the correspondence template library with activation dates.
Extract every change record in the period whose scope touched the rules table, the templates or the notice log objects.
Reconcile the change records to the table's row-level change history and investigate any table edit with no change record.
testing.done: the rules table history reconciles to the change records and unexplained edits are listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Reconcile all 51 jurisdiction rows to the Compliance requirements sheet
actions: Join the rules table export to the requirements sheet on jurisdiction code plus notice type.
Compare day count, day-count basis, anchor field, template code and effective dates field by field.
List every missing row, every mismatch and every jurisdiction defaulted to a generic rule as an exception.
testing.done: all 51 jurisdictions match the requirements sheet field for field or the differences are listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of configured rules and changes
actions: Take 100 percent of rows changed in the period and 100 percent of Alaska, Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona rows.
Take 15 further unchanged jurisdiction rows at random with a recorded seed to test that stable rows are still correct.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every changed row plus the four cited jurisdictions.

testing.step: Re-perform the day-count derivation against the statute
actions: For each sampled jurisdiction read the current statute or bulletin text and derive the notice day count, basis and anchor yourself before looking at the requirements sheet.
Compare your derivation to the sheet and to the configured row; a difference at either step is an exception.
Record the cite and the retrieval date for each derivation in the workpaper.
Flag any state that has amended its rule since the sheet was written as a configuration-overdue finding.
testing.done: each sampled jurisdiction has an independent derivation with a dated cite, compared to sheet and configuration.

testing.step: Re-execute dated scenarios in the test environment
actions: Run the auditor-supplied scenarios for the sampled jurisdictions with the system date set to a past date so the effective-dated lookup is exercised.
Compare the system-computed mail-by date and selected template edition to the auditor's expected values.
Include one late-notification scenario per sampled state to prove the notification-plus-15 alternative actually governs when it is the earlier date.
Capture the run output and the generated PDF into the workpaper.
testing.done: every re-executed scenario returns the auditor's expected mail-by date and template edition.

testing.step: Test that the enforcement controls cannot be bypassed
actions: Attempt, in the test environment, to close a notice event with an unmailed member row and confirm the system refuses.
Attempt to generate a batch with a null mandatory merge field and confirm the batch aborts rather than printing a blank.
Attempt to set a mailed-on date manually and confirm the field is not user-writable.
Attempt to issue a template before its activation date and confirm the engine blocks it.
testing.done: all four bypass attempts are blocked by the system and the refusals are captured in the workpaper.

testing.step: Trace each sampled change to test evidence and Compliance sign-off
actions: Open each sampled change record and confirm it carries the scenario results, the regression result, the Compliance UAT sign-off and the back-out export.
Confirm the UAT signer is from Compliance and is not the person who built the configuration.
Confirm the deployment date precedes the earliest state rule effective date it supports.
Treat a change deployed on a verbal or after-the-fact approval as an exception even where the configuration is correct.
testing.done: every sampled change traces to test evidence, an independent Compliance sign-off and a deployment ahead of the rule effective date.

testing.step: Verify access and monitoring on the configuration objects
actions: Pull the entitlement list for write access to the rules table and template library and compare it to the approved configuration role membership.
Confirm the last quarterly certification is complete and that leavers and movers were removed.
Confirm the four silent-failure alerts fired at least once in the period and were worked, or prove by test that they still fire.
List standing production write held by anyone outside the configuration role as an exception.
testing.done: write access matches the approved role, certification is current and each silent-failure alert is proven to fire.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a ticket per exception carrying jurisdiction, object, the configured value, the correct value and the notices already issued under the wrong value.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: requirement not received, ambiguous basis guessed, build error, released without UAT, rule amended and configuration not updated.
Set a fix release date and, where notices already went out wrong, hand the member remediation to the REG-036-C02 owner.
Carry every open ticket into the next release test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a ticket, a root cause, an owner, a fix release date and a member remediation handoff where notices were affected.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the configuration test
actions: State the count of jurisdictions matching the requirements sheet out of 51 and the count of changes with complete evidence.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — against the zero-tolerance rule on wrong day counts and missing UAT sign-off.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither built nor deployed the sampled configuration, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and the IT change board and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, a 51-jurisdiction match count and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Refresh the course content against this year's regulatory text
actions: Re-read NAIC Model #74 and the current state network adequacy standards, starting with Alaska AS 21.07.020/.030 and then Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona.
List what changed since last year's version: new day counts, new directory update cadence, new continuity of care categories, new referral cost-share rules.
Write the change list into the course change log with the citation and the retrieval date beside each item.
Hand the change list to the Instructional Designer with the slides and scenarios that must be rewritten identified by number.
checklist.done: a dated change log exists naming every content change with its citation and the affected slide or scenario.

checklist.step: Define the audience from HRIS job codes, not from last year's list
actions: Run the job-code query for in-scope populations: contact centre agents and supervisors, policy administration and correspondence staff, provider network operations, case management and utilization staff, complaints and consumer affairs, and the health product and filing team.
Include contractors and outsourced contact centre seats, which are the population most often missed.
Compare to last year's audience and investigate any job code that dropped out rather than accepting the smaller list.
Freeze the audience list with a snapshot date and store the query used to derive it.
checklist.done: the audience is derived from a stored HRIS job-code query, includes contractors, and every drop versus last year is explained.

checklist.step: Build the course around the decisions the audience actually makes
actions: Build modules for: what the time and distance and appointment wait time standards are, how to answer a member who cannot find a participating provider, when the in-network cost share applies to an out-of-network provider, how to spot a continuity of care case, how to log a directory inaccuracy and how to recognise a complaint that must be coded as network access.
Use real de-identified call transcripts and member letters rather than abstract statements of the rule.
Add the state annex covering Alaska, Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona day-count and standard differences.
Set the course to 45 minutes and version it as REG-036-NA-<year> so the completion record names the content.
checklist.done: a versioned 45-minute course exists covering the six decision points with a state annex and real scenarios.

checklist.step: Write the assessment so it tests judgement rather than recall
actions: Write 15 scenario questions with the situation described from the member's side, not the statute's.
Include at least three questions that require picking the right day count for a named state and two that require deciding whether the in-network cost share applies.
Set the pass mark at 80 percent, allow two retakes and randomise question order.
Have the Compliance Analyst mark the answer key against the citations before the course goes live.
checklist.done: a 15-question scenario assessment exists with an 80 percent pass mark and a citation-checked answer key.

checklist.step: Get the content signed off before the campaign opens
actions: Review the change log, the course and the answer key against the citations.
Confirm the state annex covers every jurisdiction where the audience actually handles members, not only the four cited examples.
Sign the content approval record naming the course version and the approval date.
Withhold approval where any change log item is not reflected in the slides.
checklist.done: a dated content approval record names the course version and confirms every change log item is reflected.

checklist.step: Assign the course in the LMS with a hard due date
actions: Load the frozen audience list as a dynamic assignment keyed on job code so movers pick it up automatically.
Launch on 1 September with a due date of 30 September and the completion window fixed at 30 days.
Configure the day 14 and day 25 learner reminders and the day 21 manager summary.
Send the launch note through the contact centre and operations leadership naming the due date and the consequence of non-completion.
checklist.done: the course is assigned to the full audience with a 30 September due date and all reminder rules live.

checklist.step: Cover new hires and movers throughout the year
actions: Configure the HRIS to LMS feed so a hire or transfer into an in-scope job code assigns the course on day one with a 30-day due date.
Run a monthly reconciliation of new in-scope job-code holders against LMS assignments and fix any that did not flow.
Add the course to the contact centre onboarding path so a new agent cannot be released to live calls without it.
Report the monthly new-hire completion rate to the Contact Center Ops Manager.
checklist.done: every in-scope hire or mover is assigned on day one and the monthly reconciliation shows no unassigned holders.

checklist.step: Chase completion through the window
actions: Publish the completion dashboard by department and manager and refresh it daily through September.
Send the manager summary at day 21 listing named non-completers rather than a percentage.
Escalate departments below 90 percent at day 25 to their operations leader.
Record the completion rate and the outstanding names at close of the window.
checklist.done: a daily dashboard runs through the window and every department below 90 percent at day 25 is escalated by name.

checklist.step: Enforce consequences on non-completers past the due date
actions: From day 31 raise a compliance exception per named non-completer with their manager and job code.
Remove non-completing contact centre agents from the network-access call queue until they complete, and record the queue change.
Escalate anyone still outstanding at day 45 to the department head and to HR through the performance route.
Close each exception only on a recorded completion with a passing score.
checklist.done: every non-completer past day 30 has an exception, a queue restriction where applicable and a day 45 escalation.

checklist.step: Handle repeated assessment failures rather than letting them pass
actions: Pull learners who failed both retakes and book each into a live coaching session within five business days.
Walk them through the questions they failed, focusing on the day-count and cost-share judgements.
Grant a supervised third attempt and record the coaching date on the learner record.
Report any learner failing after coaching to their manager for a role suitability discussion.
checklist.done: every twice-failed learner has a dated coaching session, a supervised attempt and a manager referral where they still fail.

checklist.step: Trigger an off-cycle refresh when the rules or the complaints change
actions: Watch the regulatory change feed for state bulletins tagged network adequacy and the monthly complaint theme report from Market Conduct.
Raise an off-cycle refresh where a state changes a day count or a complaint theme recurs three months running.
Issue a short module of no more than 15 minutes to the affected audience with a 14-day due date.
Log the trigger, the audience and the completion rate against the annual programme record.
checklist.done: each qualifying trigger produced a dated off-cycle module with its own audience and completion rate.

checklist.step: Measure whether the training changed behaviour
actions: Compare the network-access complaint rate and the call quality scores on network questions for the three months before and after the campaign.
Break the comparison down by team so a team that completed but did not improve is visible.
Feed the weakest topics back to the Instructional Designer as next year's content priorities.
Publish the before and after view with the annual programme record.
checklist.done: a before and after comparison by team is published and the weakest topics are handed to next year's content build.

checklist.step: Attest the year's completion
actions: Read the final completion report: audience size, completions, pass rate, outstanding names and their restrictions.
Approve or reject each requested exemption in writing with the reason, and reject any exemption for a role that handles member network-access contact.
Sign the annual attestation naming the course version, the audience size and the completion percentage.
Present the attestation to the Compliance Committee with the outstanding names.
checklist.done: a signed annual attestation exists naming course version, audience size, completion percentage and every approved exemption.

checklist.step: Retain the training evidence for the retention period
actions: Export from the LMS the per-learner completion record with name, employee id, job code, course version, score, attempt count and completion date.
File it with the course content pack, the answer key, the audience derivation query and the escalation trail under REG-036-C04 and the campaign year.
Apply the 7-years-from-training-date retention label.
Confirm the record is retrievable by learner name and by job code, which is how an exam request arrives.
checklist.done: the campaign evidence pack is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by learner name and job code.

testing.step: Build the audience population from HRIS independently of the LMS
actions: Run your own job-code query for the in-scope populations, including contractors and outsourced contact centre seats, over the whole campaign year rather than at a point in time.
Include leavers who held an in-scope code during the window, so the denominator is not quietly shrunk.
Reconcile your count to the frozen audience list and list every person you found who was never assigned.
testing.done: an independently derived audience exists and every unassigned in-scope person is listed.

testing.step: Reconcile completion records to the audience
actions: Export the LMS completion report with employee id, course version, score, attempt count and completion date.
Join it to the auditor-derived audience on employee id and compute the completion rate against the 100 percent threshold.
List completions recorded against a prior course version as exceptions — completing last year's content is not completion.
testing.done: the completion rate is computed against the auditor's audience and wrong-version completions are listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of learners
actions: Take 100 percent of non-completers, of learners with three or more attempts and of exemption holders.
Take 30 further learners at random with a recorded seed, forcing coverage of contact centre, policy administration, case management and complaints.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every non-completer, repeat failer and exemption holder.

testing.step: Re-perform the content review against the current regulatory text
actions: Read the course version delivered and check the taught day counts, directory update cadence, continuity of care periods and cost-share rule against the current statutes for Alaska, Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona.
Compare the content change log to the state changes that actually occurred in the year and list anything the course failed to pick up.
Check the state annex covers every jurisdiction the audience genuinely handles, using the contact centre call routing map.
Record each cite with its retrieval date in the workpaper.
testing.done: every taught rule is verified against current text and every missed regulatory change is listed.

testing.step: Re-mark the assessment answer key
actions: Take the 15 assessment questions and derive the correct answer yourself from the statute before opening the key.
Compare to the recorded key and treat any wrong key entry as a systemic exception affecting every learner who sat that version.
Check the pass mark is enforced at 80 percent and that retakes are capped at two before coaching.
Capture the question, the key and your derivation into the workpaper for any mismatch.
testing.done: the answer key is independently verified and any wrong entry is raised as a systemic exception.

testing.step: Trace sampled completions to the underlying LMS record
actions: Open the learner transcript for each sampled learner and read completion date, course version, score and attempt count.
Confirm the completion date falls inside the learner's own 30-day window measured from assignment or hire date.
Confirm no completion was recorded by an administrator override rather than by the learner finishing the course.
Capture the transcript screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled completion traces to a learner-generated transcript entry inside the correct window.

testing.step: Recompute the new-hire 30-day window through the year
actions: Pull every hire and transfer into an in-scope job code during the year with the effective date from HRIS.
Compute due date = start or transfer date plus 30 days and compare to the actual completion date.
List every learner who took live member calls before completing, using the contact centre queue assignment history.
Quantify the days late for each and the number of member contacts handled in the gap.
testing.done: each new hire's 30-day window is recomputed and any pre-completion member contact is quantified.

testing.step: Test the enforcement of consequences on non-completers
actions: For each non-completer confirm an exception was raised on day 31 and escalated on day 45.
Confirm contact centre non-completers were actually removed from the network-access queue by checking the queue configuration history, not only the stated intent.
Confirm each exemption carries a written reason approved by the Head of Compliance and covers no member-facing role.
Treat an exception closed without a passing completion as a fail.
testing.done: every non-completer shows an exception, a proven queue restriction where applicable and no exception closed without a pass.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an item per exception naming the learner or the systemic defect, the department and the member exposure.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: job code not in scope query, HRIS feed failure, content missed a rule change, wrong answer key, manager did not release time, queue restriction not applied.
Set a remediation date, reassign the course where content was wrong, and require re-completion by the whole affected cohort where the key was wrong.
Carry every open item into next year's campaign as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an item, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a cohort re-completion where content was defective.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the training test
actions: State the completion rate against the auditor-derived audience, the pass rate and the count of learners who handled member contact without completion.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — against the 100 percent completion and 80 percent pass thresholds.
Have the independent reviewer, from outside Compliance and Learning and Development, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, completion rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.
