checklist.step: Set the network-access reason codes that make the complaints findable
actions: Create six reason codes: no participating provider within the time and distance standard, appointment wait beyond the standard, provider directory listing inaccurate, member balance-billed after using a listed provider, out-of-network referral request denied, continuity of care request denied.
Map each code to the NAIC complaint reason and coverage type codes so the case can be reported without re-keying.
Publish the coding rules with a worked example per code to the contact centre and complaints teams.
Turn off any legacy generic 'network' code so it cannot be selected.
checklist.done: the six codes are live, NAIC-mapped, documented with examples and the generic legacy code is disabled.

checklist.step: Ingest complaints from every channel into one register
actions: Load Division inquiries daily from the NAIC Complaints Database System and from each state portal that does not feed it, capturing the Division file number and the stated response due date.
Load member complaints from the portal form, the complaints mailbox and the contact centre escalation queue.
Pull the contact centre disposition report for network-access calls and open a case for any that meets the complaint definition but never became one.
Set the register key to Division file number where one exists so the same matter is never double-counted.
checklist.done: all four channels land in one register with Division file numbers captured and no duplicate matters.

checklist.step: Triage and code each complaint within one business day
actions: Read the complaint text and set the reason code from the six, the state of issue, the product, the county and the specialty involved.
Set the response clock: the Division's stated due date, or 15 calendar days where none is stated, and 30 calendar days for a member complaint.
Send the member acknowledgement within 5 business days naming the case reference and the handler.
Route the case to the handler queue by state and code, and flag any complaint alleging a delay in urgent care for same-day clinical review.
checklist.done: every complaint is coded, clocked, acknowledged within 5 business days and routed, with urgent-care allegations flagged same day.

checklist.step: Re-test the adequacy standard for the member who complained
actions: Run the network adequacy query for the member's address, plan and the specialty in question, returning participating providers by driving distance and accepting-new-patients status.
Compare the result to the state's time and distance standard for that county designation (large metro, metro, micro, rural, counties with extreme access considerations).
For appointment wait complaints call the two nearest listed providers and record the next available appointment date offered, and compare to the state's wait time standard.
Write the finding on the case as MET or NOT MET with the query output and the call notes attached.
checklist.done: every case carries a MET or NOT MET adequacy finding with the query output and, for wait complaints, dated call notes.

checklist.step: Resolve the member's immediate problem before arguing about the standard
actions: Where the finding is NOT MET, authorise the out-of-network provider at the in-network cost share and load the authorization with the approved services and period.
Where the member was balance-billed after relying on the directory, open a claim reprocessing request at the in-network benefit and record the dollar amount.
Where a continuity of care request was wrongly denied, reinstate the transitional period from the original termination date and reprocess the affected claims.
Call the member with the outcome and follow with the written response inside the response clock.
checklist.done: every NOT MET case has an authorization or reprocessing action with a dollar amount, plus a call and a written response inside the clock.

checklist.step: Answer the Division on its own terms and by its own date
actions: Draft the response answering each numbered question the Division asked, in its order, with the adequacy query output and the member remediation attached.
State the standard applied and the citation, and state plainly where the standard was not met rather than describing process.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear any response that concedes an adequacy failure or describes a pattern.
Upload through the NAIC Complaints Database System or the state portal and save the confirmation with its timestamp on the case.
checklist.done: every Division inquiry has a filed response, a saved upload confirmation and counsel clearance where a failure was conceded.

checklist.step: Assign a root cause that a network manager can act on
actions: Assign a cause from the fixed list: genuine network gap in the county and specialty, provider closed to new patients but shown as open, directory data stale, provider terminated and members not notified, referral rules misapplied by staff, member misunderstood the benefit.
Record the county, specialty and network id on every case so causes aggregate to something addressable.
Where the cause is a genuine gap, raise a network gap item to Provider Network Operations with the county, specialty, member count and the standard being missed.
Where the cause is staff error, raise a coaching item to the Contact Center Ops Manager naming the agent and the call.
checklist.done: every case has a fixed-list cause with county, specialty and network id, and a gap or coaching item where applicable.

checklist.step: Work the daily SLA breach list before cases go late
actions: Open the complaint SLA dashboard each morning and read the Division inquiries due in 3, 2 and 1 days and the member cases at day 20 and day 28.
Reassign any case whose handler is absent and record the reassignment on the case.
Escalate any Division inquiry inside 2 days of its due date to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager the same morning.
Record the reason on any case that breached — evidence not returned by claims, member unreachable, provider data query outstanding.
checklist.done: no Division inquiry passes its due date without escalation and every breach carries a recorded reason.

checklist.step: Trend the network-access book monthly
actions: Build the monthly view: complaints per 1,000 members by state, by reason code, by county and by specialty, with a rolling three-month trend.
Highlight any county and specialty pair with three or more complaints in a rolling quarter as a hot spot.
Overlay the network gap items already raised so a hot spot with no open gap item is visible.
Publish to Compliance, Provider Network Operations and the Chief Claims Officer by the fifth working day of each month.
checklist.done: the monthly view is published by working day five with hot spots identified and unmatched gap items visible.

checklist.step: Drive the network remediation the complaints are pointing at
actions: Open a remediation item per hot spot naming county, specialty, complaint count and the standard being missed.

Agree with Provider Network Operations one of three actions: recruit named providers, file an access plan justification with the state, or apply a standing out-of-network at in-network cost share arrangement for that county and specialty.
Set a target date and a monthly checkpoint, and require the complaint rate for that pair to be reported at each checkpoint.
Close the item only when the complaint rate falls for two consecutive months or the state accepts the justification.
checklist.done: every hot spot has an owned remediation with a named action, a target date and a complaint rate closing condition.

checklist.step: Reconcile the register to the Division's own complaint counts
actions: Pull the Division's complaint listing for the company from the NAIC Complaints Database System for the period.
Match each Division record to a register case on Division file number and investigate every Division record with no internal case.
Check the reason code the Division applied against the code the company applied and reconcile the differences.
Correct the register and record the reconciliation as evidence for the MCAS submission.
checklist.done: every Division complaint record matches an internal case and reason code differences are reconciled and documented.

checklist.step: Feed the counts into the annual MCAS Health filing
actions: Extract the complaint counts by state and reason for the data year and map them to the MCAS Health complaint elements.
Reconcile the extract to the register and to the Division listing before loading, and document any deliberate difference.
Submit through NAIC iSite+ MCAS by the 30 April deadline for the prior data year and save the submission confirmation.
File the reconciliation and the confirmation with the MCAS evidence pack.
checklist.done: MCAS Health complaint counts are reconciled, submitted by 30 April and the confirmation is filed.

checklist.step: Report the network-access picture to governance
actions: Take to the quarterly Compliance Committee: complaint volume and rate trend, confirmed access failures, open hot spots, member remediation dollars and Division response performance.
Name the counties and specialties that have been open for more than two quarters and the reason.
Record committee decisions and owners in the minutes and reflect them on the remediation items.
Escalate to the board risk committee any state where confirmed access failures are trending up for three consecutive quarters.
checklist.done: the quarterly report is delivered with named long-open hot spots and minuted decisions carried back to the remediation items.

checklist.step: Retain the complaint evidence for the retention period
actions: Archive each closed case file — original complaint, adequacy query output, call notes, authorization or reprocessing record, response letter and Division correspondence — under REG-036-C05 and the closure quarter.
Apply the 10-years-from-closure retention label to cover the market conduct exam look-back.
Confirm the archive is searchable by Division file number, member id, state, county and reason code.
Spot-check one archived case per quarter by opening it end to end.
checklist.done: closed cases are archived, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by Division file number and reason code.

testing.step: Build the complaint population from more than the complaint register
actions: Extract every case closed in the quarter from the complaint register with state, reason code, dates and outcome.
Add the contact centre disposition extract for network-access calls and the Division listing from the NAIC Complaints Database System.
Reconcile the three sources and list every Division record or escalated call that never became a register case as a completeness exception.
testing.done: the population is built from three independent sources and every unregistered matter is listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the reason coding against the complaint text
actions: Read the free-text complaint for 40 cases coded outside the six network-access codes and judge whether they should have been coded as network access.
Compare the company reason code to the Division's own code on every matter that came through the Division.
List every mis-coded case, since mis-coding removes the complaint from the trend and from MCAS.
Quantify the effect of the mis-coding on the quarter's network-access complaint count.
testing.done: mis-coded cases are identified from the text and the effect on the reported count is quantified.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of complaints
actions: Take 100 percent of Division inquiries, of NOT MET findings and of Alaska cases as the representative jurisdiction.
Take 30 further cases at random with a recorded seed spread across the six reason codes.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every Division inquiry and every NOT MET finding.

testing.step: Re-perform the adequacy determination for each sampled case
actions: Run the network adequacy query yourself for the member's address, plan and specialty as at the complaint date, and reach your own MET or NOT MET conclusion before reading the case finding.
Read the state's standard for that county designation from the current text rather than from the internal standards table, and note the cite.
Compare to the recorded finding; a difference is an exception, including a MET call resting on a provider who was closed to new patients.
Capture the query output and the standard into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled case has an independent adequacy conclusion with a cited standard and captured query output.

testing.step: Recompute the response clocks and test the SLA maths
actions: For Division inquiries recompute due date from the date received and the Division's stated due date, defaulting to 15 calendar days where none is stated.
For member complaints recompute acknowledgement due at 5 business days and resolution due at 30 calendar days from receipt.
Compare to the actual acknowledgement, response and closure dates from the case audit trail rather than the summary fields.
List every breach with days late and check whether the case was reopened after closure, which hides a breach.
testing.done: every clock is recomputed from the audit trail and each breach is quantified in days late.

testing.step: Trace the member remediation to a real claim or authorization
actions: For each NOT MET case open the authorization and confirm it exists, names the approved provider and services, and covers the dates the member needed.
Pull the claims for the sampled member in the period and confirm they priced at the in-network cost share.
For balance-bill cases confirm the reprocessing actually paid and the member refund or provider adjustment cleared, with the dollar amount.
List any promised remediation with no matching claim or payment record.
testing.done: every promised remediation traces to an authorization or a settled claim with a dollar amount.

testing.step: Test the Division response content and the filing confirmation
actions: Open each sampled Division response and confirm it answers every numbered question in the inquiry.
Confirm the standard cited in the response matches the standard the auditor verified for that state and county designation.
Confirm the upload confirmation timestamp is on or before the Division due date.
Confirm Regulatory Counsel cleared any response conceding an adequacy failure, with the clearance dated before the upload.
testing.done: every sampled response is complete, correctly cited, filed on time and counsel-cleared where required.

testing.step: Test that root causes converted into network action
actions: Take every county and specialty pair with three or more complaints in the rolling quarter and check a remediation item exists.
Read the agreed action and confirm it is one of recruit, file an access plan justification, or apply a standing out-of-network at in-network arrangement — not 'monitor'.
Check the complaint rate reported at the last checkpoint and whether the closing condition was actually met before closure.
List hot spots open more than two quarters with no change in complaint rate as a systemic finding.
testing.done: every hot spot has a real action and no item is closed without its complaint-rate closing condition being met.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an item per exception carrying case reference, state, county, specialty, days late or dollar impact.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: not registered, mis-coded, adequacy re-test not run, wrong standard applied, remediation promised not delivered, Division response late.
Set a remediation date, and where a member was left out of pocket require the reprocessing before closure.
Carry every open item into the next month's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an item, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the complaint monitoring test
actions: State the Division on-time rate against 100 percent, the member 30-day rate against 95 percent and the count of confirmed access failures without remediation.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who handled none of the sampled complaints, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, the hot spot list and the member remediation total to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, both SLA rates and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Risk assess and scope the engagement
actions: Read the prior year issues, the network-access complaint trend from Market Conduct and the notice past-due history from the aging dashboard to rank the states and notice types by risk.

Write the scope statement naming the notice types in scope, the states subject to 100 percent coverage, the audit year period and the four processes covered (content build, generation and delivery, system configuration, training).
Confirm no team member worked in Compliance or Policy Administration in the last 12 months and record the independence confirmations.
Issue the engagement letter to the Head of Compliance, the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Head of IT with the fieldwork dates.
checklist.done: an approved scope statement, dated independence confirmations and an issued engagement letter exist.

checklist.step: Re-base the audit programme on primary regulatory sources
actions: Read NAIC Model #74 notice, directory and continuity of care sections and the network adequacy statutes for the in-scope states, starting with Alaska AS 21.07.020/.030 then Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona.
Build the audit criteria table: one row per state per notice type with day count, day-count basis, anchor and mandatory content elements, each with a cite and retrieval date.
Deliberately build the table from the statutes rather than from the Compliance requirements sheet, then note where the two differ as a preliminary finding.
Have a second auditor review the criteria table before fieldwork opens.
checklist.done: a peer-reviewed criteria table exists built from primary sources with every difference from the Compliance sheet noted.

checklist.step: Build and reconcile the notice population
actions: Extract every network adequacy notice issued in the audit year from the correspondence archive with member id, state, letter code, edition, generation and mailed-on dates.
Extract the provider termination history and the continuity of care case list separately and join them to the notice extract.
Reconcile: every termination with impacted members must have notices, and every notice must trace to an event; investigate both directions.
Sign the population as complete and record the reconciliation differences before sampling.
checklist.done: the notice population reconciles in both directions to the termination history and is signed as complete.

checklist.step: Design and draw the statistical sample
actions: Set the sampling plan: 95 percent confidence, 5 percent tolerable rate, attribute sampling for content and timing, and record the resulting size.
Stratify by state risk rank and notice type, taking 100 percent of Alaska, Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona and of all late or RED events.
Draw the sample with a recorded seed and store the drawn list in the engagement file.
Record the population size, sample size, seed and draw date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
checklist.done: the sample is drawn from a documented statistical plan and is reproducible from the recorded seed.

checklist.step: Test the content of each sampled notice against the criteria table
actions: Open the archived member copy — not the template — for each sampled notice.

Tick each mandatory element from the criteria table row for that state: provider name and specialty, termination effective date, two named alternatives with addresses, transition request number, continuity of care rights and period, out-of-network cost share rule and the complaint route.
Record the form number and edition on the copy and check it against the approved edition list for that state on the mailing date.
Photograph or capture the copy into the test sheet for every exception.
checklist.done: each sampled notice has a completed element tick-list and a verified template edition, with captures for every exception.

checklist.step: Test the timing of each sampled notice
actions: Recompute mail-by date from the criteria table day count and the anchor, and compute days-early against the mailed-on date.
Take the mailed-on date from the mail vendor manifest, never from the system summary field.
For e-delivered notices take the portal post timestamp and the email delivery status.
Record days-early, the source of the date and the exception status on the test sheet.
checklist.done: every sampled notice has a recomputed days-early figure sourced from a vendor manifest or portal audit record.

checklist.step: Test the delivery and the undeliverable trail
actions: Confirm the mailing address used matches the address of record on the mailing date.
For returned pieces confirm an address correction attempt and a re-mail inside three business days, or two logged alternative contact attempts before an Undeliverable mark.
Check whether a better address existed in claims or premium records at the time of the return.
Record each failure as a delivery exception distinct from a timing exception.
checklist.done: delivery exceptions are recorded separately from timing exceptions with the address evidence attached.

checklist.step: Test the enforcing system configuration behind the notices
actions: Export the jurisdiction rules table and compare all 51 rows to the audit criteria table field by field.
Observe the operator attempt to close an event with an unmailed member and to generate a batch with a null merge field, and record the system's refusal.
Confirm the mailed-on date field is not user-writable and that row-level change history is on.
Trace three configuration changes in the year to a change record with Compliance UAT sign-off.
checklist.done: the 51 rules rows are compared to audit criteria, the bypass attempts are observed to fail and three changes trace to approved records.

checklist.step: Test the training that supports correct notice handling
actions: Derive the in-scope audience from HRIS job codes and reconcile it to the LMS assignment list.
Compute the completion rate against the auditor-derived audience and check ten transcripts for course version, score and completion date inside the learner window.
Read three assessment questions against the criteria table to confirm the taught day counts are the current ones.
Record any learner who handled member network-access contact without a completion.
checklist.done: the completion rate is recomputed against an HRIS-derived audience and taught day counts are verified against audit criteria.

checklist.step: Quantify the member impact of every exception
actions: For each missing or late notice count the members affected and pull their claims to the terminated provider in the affected window.
Compute the additional member cost share paid because the notice or the continuity of care offer was missed.
Separate quantified financial harm from access harm — a member who could not find a provider is an impact even with no claim.
Total the impact by state so the report can speak in the terms a Division will ask about.
checklist.done: every exception carries a member count and, where applicable, a dollar impact totalled by state.

checklist.step: Rate the findings and write them up
actions: Rate each finding High, Medium or Low using the engagement rating scale, and rate any missing notice or unapproved template edition High by rule.
Write each finding as condition, criteria with cite, cause, effect with the quantified impact, and recommendation.
Attach the test sheets and captures that support the finding.
Have a second auditor review each write-up for evidence sufficiency before it goes to management.
checklist.done: every finding is rated, written to the five-part standard, evidenced and peer reviewed.

checklist.step: Take management responses and agree owned actions
actions: Issue the draft report to the Head of Compliance, the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Head of IT with responses due in 10 business days.
Hold the closing meeting and challenge any response that accepts the risk without a fix on a High finding.
Record for each finding the agreed action, the named owner and the due date, and reject actions that read as 'reinforce the procedure'.
Escalate any unresolved disagreement on a High finding to the Audit Committee chair before the report is finalised.
checklist.done: every finding has a written management response with a named owner, a dated action and no unfixed High finding accepted silently.

checklist.step: Issue the report and take it to the Audit Committee
actions: Finalise the report with scope, population and sample sizes, content and timing exception rates, quantified member impact and the overall opinion.
Issue within 15 business days of fieldwork close to management and to the Compliance Committee.
Present at the Q1 Audit Committee sitting with the High findings and the prior-year overdue issues named.
File the report and the engagement file in the audit platform and cross-file to the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the final report is issued within 15 business days, presented to the Audit Committee and filed in both repositories.

checklist.step: Follow up and re-test the fixes rather than accepting assertions
actions: Track each action to its due date on the issue log and chase the owner 10 business days before it falls due.
On the owner's completion claim, re-test on live data: pull notices issued after the fix and re-run the content and timing tests on a small sample.
Close the issue only where the re-test passes; where it fails, reopen with the original rating and report it as overdue.
Report the overdue High issue list to the Audit Committee at every sitting until it is empty.
checklist.done: no issue is closed without a live-data re-test and every overdue High issue is on the committee list.

checklist.step: Retain the engagement file for the retention period
actions: Archive the criteria table, population extract and reconciliation, sampling evidence, test sheets, issue log, management responses and final report under REG-036-C06 and the audit year.
Apply the 7-years-from-report-issue retention label.
Confirm the file is retrievable by audit year, state and finding rating.
Confirm the sampling seed and population extract are present so a third party could redraw the sample.
checklist.done: the engagement file is archived, labelled for 7-year retention and contains everything needed to redraw the sample.

testing.step: Rebuild the notice population independently of the audit team
actions: Extract the audit year's provider termination history and impacted-member attribution yourself and derive the expected notice count.
Compare it to the population the audit used and investigate any shortfall in the audit population.
List any notice type or state the audit scope excluded and assess whether the exclusion was justified in the scope statement.
testing.done: the audit population is reconciled to an independently derived expected count and every scope exclusion is assessed.

testing.step: Reconcile the audit criteria table to the current statutes
actions: Read the network adequacy notice provisions for Alaska, Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona and derive day count, basis, anchor and mandatory content yourself.
Compare to the audit criteria table row by row and note any criterion that was too lenient, which would have suppressed findings.
Confirm each criteria row carries a cite and a retrieval date inside the audit year.
Record the derivation and the cite in the review workpaper.
testing.done: the criteria table is verified against current statutes and any lenient criterion is raised.

testing.step: Redraw the sample from the recorded seed
actions: Re-run the sampling routine with the recorded seed and population extract and compare the drawn list to the list tested.
Confirm the sample size matches the documented 95 percent confidence and 5 percent tolerable rate plan.
Confirm the 100 percent strata — the four cited states and all late or RED events — were fully covered rather than sampled.
List any tested item that is not in the redrawn sample as a sampling integrity exception.
testing.done: the redrawn sample matches the tested list and the 100 percent strata are proven complete.

testing.step: Re-perform the content test on a subset of the audit sample
actions: Take 15 notices from the audit sample and open the archived member copies yourself.
Tick the mandatory elements from the counsel-verified criteria without reading the auditor's test sheet first.
Compare your conclusion to the auditor's and treat any element the auditor passed but you fail as a review exception.
Capture the copy and both conclusions into the review workpaper.
testing.done: 15 notices are independently content-tested and every difference from the auditor's conclusion is recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the timing maths and the date sourcing
actions: Recompute mail-by and days-early for the same 15 notices from the counsel-verified day counts.
Confirm the auditor took mailed-on dates from the vendor manifest by opening the manifest line yourself.
Check whether any exception was cleared on a system summary field rather than a manifest date.
Recompute the reported timing exception rate from the sample results and compare to the rate in the report.
testing.done: the timing maths and the reported exception rate are independently recomputed from manifest-sourced dates.

testing.step: Verify the quantified member impact
actions: For the five largest quantified findings pull the underlying member claims and recompute the additional cost share paid.
Confirm the population of affected members matches the notice exception rather than a broader or narrower set.
Confirm access harm without a dollar value was still counted and described rather than dropped.
Record the recomputed totals beside the reported totals by state.
testing.done: the five largest impact figures are recomputed from claims and reconciled to the reported totals.

testing.step: Test that findings were rated and written to the standard
actions: Read every finding and confirm it carries condition, criteria with cite, cause, quantified effect and recommendation.
Confirm every missing notice and every unapproved template edition was rated High as the rating rule requires.
Confirm the peer review is evidenced on each write-up and predates issue to management.
List any finding downgraded between draft and final and read the justification.
testing.done: every finding meets the five-part standard, mandatory High ratings were applied and any downgrade is justified in writing.

testing.step: Test the follow-up closures on live data
actions: Take every issue closed in the period and check the closure evidence is a post-fix live-data re-test, not a management assertion or a project plan.
Re-run the content and timing test on three notices issued after each claimed fix.
Reopen any issue whose re-test fails and check whether the original rating was restored.
Confirm overdue High issues appeared on every Audit Committee pack until closure.
testing.done: every closure rests on a post-fix live-data re-test and overdue High issues are traced through the committee packs.

testing.step: Log every review exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a quality item per review exception naming the engagement step, the effect on the opinion and the finding it would have changed.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: population incomplete, criteria too lenient, sample not covering the mandatory strata, evidence not sourced independently, finding under-rated, closure without re-test.
Set a remediation date and, where the opinion is affected, require a supplementary report to the Audit Committee.
Carry every open quality item into next year's engagement planning as a mandatory scope item.
testing.done: every review exception has an item, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a scope commitment for next year.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the audit quality review
actions: State whether the recomputed content and timing exception rates support the opinion issued.
Write the conclusion — the audit is relied upon, relied upon with qualification, or not relied upon — with the review workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed none of the fieldwork, sign the review workpaper.
Report the review outcome to the Audit Committee alongside the engagement report and file both in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed review workpaper with a stated reliance conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.
